extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: Visual Question Answering (VQA) entails answering questions about images. We introduce the first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: From the Stack Exchange archive, we collected all examples containing four components: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We conducted two filtering steps to obtain our final dataset of 64,696 VQAs. First, we removed low-quality VQAs based on Stack Exchange’s feature that enables users to up-vote or down-vote each post... Second, we excluded visual questions with multiple images ( e.g., GIF) or with visual answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance (i.e. image-question-context-answer) for 105 randomly selected VQAs, one from each of 105 topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We found that 25 out of 105 didn’t match. Thus, we hired a third worker (worker C) to break the tie by instructing that individual to select one of the two provided user intentions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: VQAonline supports few-shot leaming by containing training, validation, and test splits

name.evidence: We introduce a new dataset called VQAonline.

description.evidence: Visual Question Answering (VQA) entails answering questions about images. We introduce the first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.

url.evidence: We publicly-share the dataset at: https://vqaonline.github.io/.

license.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022, and adhered to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0) set forth by Stack Exchange.

creator.evidence: Chongyan Chen1, Mengchen Liu2, Noel Codella2, Yunsheng Li2, Lu Yuan2, and Danna Gurari1,3

inLanguage.evidence: most of our visual questions are written in English

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: From the Stack Exchange archive, we collected all examples containing four components: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We conducted two filtering steps to obtain our final dataset of 64,696 VQAs . First, we removed low-quality VQAs based on Stack Exchange’s feature that enables users to up-vote or down-vote each post (either question or answer)... Second, we excluded visual questions with multiple images ( e.g., GIF) or with visual answers.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance (i.e. image-question-context-answer) for 105 randomly selected VQAs, one from each of 105 topics.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We found that 25 out of 105 didn’t match. Thus, we hired a third worker (worker C) to break the tie by instructing that individual to select one of the two provided user intentions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: we only accepted workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We utilized the state-of-the-art text spotter model DeepSolo to detect text for all images in our dataset.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Additionally, the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: VQAonline supports few-shot leaming by containing training, validation, and test splits of 665, 285, and 63,746 examples respectively.
